newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden may look at wealth tax on shares soon.
newsitem.headline: Sweden may look at wealth tax on shares soon.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday that the government could look at possibly changing a wealth tax on company owners this autumn.

"This is something that we will look at and it is possible that we will came back later in the autumn with some kind of proposal," Asbrink told jounalists after a Social Democratic party economic seminar.
Since June a list of Swedish companies have moved their shares from the Stockholm bourse's main A-list to the smaller O-list to avoid the wealth tax.
A 1996 law forces Swedes with wealth exceeding 900,000 crowns to pay 1.5 percent tax on 100 percent of the value of shares listed on the A-list. O-list shares are exempt.

The recent share transfers were triggered by a law adopted by parliament in June reaffirming that main shareholders in companies have to pay tax for shares listed on the A list before 1991. Companies had hoped parliament would change the 1996 law.
The law has caused companies like fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, media group Marieberg, construction group Lundbergs and investment companies Latour and Custos to flee from the A to the O list.
Asbrink said he was not that concerned about companies moving to the O-list.
"You can always debate how big a problem it is for a company to move its shares from one list to another," he said.
But he questioned if having different tax rules on different lists was the best possible method.
"If there is something that is wrong we shall correct it," Asbrink said.
